hypothesis: The Mockito framework incorrectly records the invocation of 'mock.otherMethod()' when it is passed as an argument to 'verify(mockTwo).simpleMethod(...)'. Because this invocation is recorded, a subsequent 'verify(mockTwo, never()).simpleMethod(mock.otherMethod())' fails because it detects that 'mock.otherMethod()' was indeed called (during the evaluation of the argument in the previous verification line).
prediction: The invocation recording mechanism fails to ignore calls made during the evaluation of verification arguments.

This is a classic issue of the framework's internal state management (the recording algorithm) failing to account for side effects of argument evaluation.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by the framework's inability to distinguish between actual test interactions and interactions caused by evaluating arguments within a verification call. This is a procedural flaw in how Mockito records invocations, fitting the Algorithm/Method category as it requires a change to the invocation recording logic.
